chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, who said:

I wrote to Abu Muhammad (peace be upon him): A man had two sons, so one of them died, and he left behind male and female children. So their grandfather bequeathed to them the portion of their father. Is this portion such that the male and the female are equal in it, or does the male have the share of two females? He (peace be upon him) signed: 'They enforce the bequest of their grandfather just as he ordered, God willing.'

He said: And I wrote to him: A man had male and female children, so he acknowledged for them a property that it is for his children, and did not mention that it is to be divided between them according to the shares of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and His obligations. Is the male and the female equal in it? He (peace be upon him) signed: 'They enforce in it the bequest of their father upon what he named. So if he had not named anything, they return it to the Book of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and the Sunnah of His Prophet (peace be upon him and his family), God willing.'
ai.seo_question: How is a grandfather's bequest enforced if he does not specify the exact shares for male and female heirs?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the principle of *al-wasiyyah* (bequest) within the family, establishing that a testator's specific designation overrides the default Quranic inheritance shares (*fara'id*) provided it does not exceed one-third of the estate. The Imam distinguishes between explicit stipulations of equality versus silence, where the latter defaults to the standard male-double-female ratio, reflecting the Shia scholarly emphasis on the flexibility of testamentary freedom within the bounds of Sharia. This ruling underscores the practical application of Quranic verses on bequests, balancing individual intent with communal inheritance norms.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad who said,

‘I wrote to Abu Muhammad<sup>asws</sup>, ‘A man had two sons for him, so one of them died having (left behind) a boy and a girl. So their grandfather bequeathed to them with the portion of their father. So in this portion, the male and the female are equal in it, or for the male would be similar to two females?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> signed: ‘The bequest of their grandfather would be enforced just as he had ordered, Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Willing’.

He (the narrator) said, ‘And I wrote to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘A man who had children, male and female, so he agreed for then with a place that it is for his children, and did not mention that it is (to be divided) between them with the share (Prescribed by) Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic, and His<sup>azwj</sup> Obligation. The male and the female are equal in it?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> signed: ‘The bequest of their father would be enforced upon what he has named. So if he had not mentioned anything, so refer it to the Book of Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic, and the Sunnah of His<sup>azwj</sup> Prophet<sup>saww</sup>, Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Willing’.
en.sarwar: 1. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad who has narrated the following: “I once wrote to abu Muhammad, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, and asked about the case of a man who has two sons. One of them dies, leaving behind male and female children, and the grandfather bequests for them the share of their father, if male and female in this share are equal or if the male has twice the share of the female. He (the Imam), ‘Alayhi al-Salam, signed the answer that said, ‘The will of their grandfather must be executed by the will of Allah.’

He (the narrator) has said that a man wrote to him (the Imam) about the case of a man who has male and female children and he confirms that a piece of property belongs to his children without mentioning if it is according to the share Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious, has determined or male and female share it equally.’

He (the Imam) signed the answer that said, ‘They must execute the will of their father according to what he has mentioned. However, if he has not mentioned anything they must refer to the book of Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious, and the Sunnah of the Holy Prophet, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, by the will of Allah.’”
